Your domestic helper is entitled to long service payment if he/she has worked for you for at least 5 years before termination and you do not renew the contract for reasons other than misconduct and redundancy.
If your domestic helper resigns due to his/her ill health, you need to pay for his/her long service.

[11/11/2020, 8:06:06 PM] Clodagh: Increase in seasonal upper respiratory infections in Hong Kong
Dear Parents
 
We are aware of a number of school closures in Hong Kong at this time, due to an increase in upper respiratory infections in their populations.  We are monitoring the situation closely and are in continual contact with the Centre for Health Protection (CHP).  At this time, DBIS will remain open across all phases of the school.
 
Hong Kong is entering into the time of year where common cold symptoms arise with more frequency. There has been an increase in such cold symptoms at school, this includes: nasal congestion, sore throat, runny nose, fatigue, pressure in facial sinuses and headache.
 
The CHP has advised that anyone with such symptoms should inform the school and rest at home.  Students may return to school 48 hours after symptoms have subsided.
 
The common cold has similar symptoms to COVID-19. The CHP advises that anyone with a fever, respiratory symptoms (cough, breathing difficulties) and/or loss of sense of taste/smell should consult a doctor prior to returning to school.
 
Could you ensure your children continue to perform regular hand hygiene and ensure they wear a fresh mask daily. If reusable masks are used, ensure that they are washed every day.
 
Please be assured that the school is continuing to carry out a stringent cleaning routine throughout the school day, whilst enforcing the necessary social distance protocols including mask wearing, hand sanitising and plastic screens. 
 
We will continue to monitor the situation at DBIS and will inform you if there are any further developments.
 
Kind regards
 
Stuart Bridge

Hi Sophia!
Thank you for joining our Kapuhala CNY Camp.

Meet up : Kapuhala Promenade near the roundabout going to the North Plaza Beach.

Drop Off Time : 1025

Pick up Time :
12:30
At Kapuhala Promenade Area

Some of the activities covered:
1. Warm up / circuit style workout/ running
2. Tag game. i.e. Spider-Man/ Red light Green light
3. Rob the nest
4. Obstacle course
5. Relay races with cones & ball
6. Shuttle runs 
7. Outdoor explorations
8) Tug of war
9) Marco Polo
10) around DB hike


Activities are held outdoors and there will be water breaks to make sure kids are hydrated.

Our aim is to find ways for kids to enjoy physical fitness by using fun game activities as a mean to stepping in to what a life long fitness journey will create.

Together we build passion, teamwork, drive and critical thinking under pressure as a team or individual. Kids will get a chance to socialise and make friends! 

Things to bring:
- Water bottle 
- Snacks
- Sunblock
- Raincoat
- A change of clothes would be useful just in case they get wet.

The Kapuhala Team

[20/4/2022, 8:29:16 PM] Julian: *Covid Measures* 
Thank you to everyone who has been in touch to confirm and sign up for the new term. A few important notes as we prepare the start next week:

1. The first day of the reopening of the courts will be Thursday 21st April which will also be the first day/class of our junior tennis programme. Other classes will start following that day so first Friday classes will be on Friday 22nd April, first Monday classes will be on 25th April etc. 

2. In case anyone has made any changes to their membership status or numbers since January, please let me know.

3. Members who do not have credit on their accounts should make the payment for lessons directly at the club front desk on the same day as the lesson and send me a photo of the receipt directly for confirmation

4. In regards to Covid measures:
- Classes will be run with a maximum 4 players + 1 coach per court and 1.5m distance will be kept between players and coaches or subgroups of 4 people. 
- Face masks are required to be worn at all times including during lessons. (There are some great sports masks which are much more breathable and easier to use for sports).
- All persons must have received 1st dose of COVID-19 vaccination before 29th April, 2022 (or be medically exempt or below 12 years old)
- All persons using the Club must present a valid vaccination record QR code or medical exemption for scanning at the Clubhouse Main Entrance, either electronic or paper copy. If you are unable to provide valid proof of vaccination, the Club will deny entry as per   Government Vaccine Pass regulations;
- All persons must scan the LeaveHomeSafe QR code using the LeaveHomeSafe mobile application before entering to club facilities (except those who are below 16 years old accompanied by an adult)
- Mandatory temperature checked and to complete a Health Declaration Form. A form must be submitted per person per visit and ready at entrance area.

*Junior Tennis Programme General Terms and Conditions*

1. Once the programme starts and the student’s spot is confirmed, lessons run on a weekly basis. 
2. After confirmation of lesson, failure to attend the lesson for any reason in no way absolves the participant from the financial obligation. No refunds or credit will be provided. 
3. In case a student is unable to attend a lesson for any reason, notice should be given to the coach directly and a make-up lesson on another day may be offered subject to availability of spaces. 
4. There will be no lessons  on Sundays. Lessons on Public Holidays are optional and made by special arrangement. 
5. Lesson charges will be refunded for lessons cancelled by the Club or the Coach due to adverse weather or for any other reasons.
6. Lessons are cancelled if the general AQI PM2.5 level exceeds 200 or AQHI reaches level 10. 
7. Participants who wish to discontinue must give at least 2 weeks notice directly to the coach.

See you soon to work hard and have fun.🎾

[22/7/2022, 12:14:50 AM] Clodagh: A week ago today we made the tough decision to close our doors permanently after 16 years of operations. It has taken me a week to be able to gather my thoughts and get through what has possibly been the most painful time in my life both mentally and physically, and for this radio silence I apologize. 

Hemingway’s joins the ever-growing list of venues to close down across Hong Kong. The past two and a half years have made it almost impossible to run a food and beverage business here. The lethal combination of Government covid restrictions, a greed driven inflexible landlord and the exodus of clientele sealed our fate. 

Live music was what made Hemingway’s tick, accounting for 40% of our revenue. Without Live music as you can imagine finances became very tough. Add to that the many ridiculous, illogical Govt restrictions such as RAT tests at a bar counter, yet no RAT tests at a table 2m away meant no bar patrons and no atmosphere. These restrictions have also been responsible for the exodus of our clientele, many of whom were long term Hong Kong residents but simply ‘had enough’.

Some venues have managed to survive in the city largely due to understanding landlords who realized that they too needed to shoulder some of the burden and give reduced rental relief assistance throughout the two and a half years, to ensure they have a tenant coming out the other side. Sadly this is not the case in Discovery Bay where our landlord insists there was no change in business levels therefore no rental reduction, despite reducing ferries and buses to save costs due to a downturn in business demands amongst many other things. I pray that karma will take care of them!

As a family-owned business as opposed to a large restaurant group, my wife and I have ploughed all of our personal savings into the business on the hope that we were almost through covid and brighter days were ahead. We have amassed huge personal debts that became unbearable and sadly the accounts are all empty. Cash flow has stopped flowing which is the death of any business.

We have taken care of our beloved staff financially, and tried to satisfy as many suppliers as we could but not all will regrettably get their full amount owed. We can only hope that the 16 years of loyal custom accounts for something.

Hong Kong is an expensive city to live in, and with no income we decided to leave for the UK after 32 years in this wonderful city. I wish HK all the best in its future and hope one day to return for a visit.

My parting advice for what it’s worth, to anyone considering opening a food and beverage venue anywhere in Hong Kong….. 
ASK WHAT YOUR FUTURE LANDLORD DID FOR THEIR TENANTS DURING THE COVID YEARS. This will give you a very good indication of their character and how you will be treated should we hit tough times. 

From Gary, Margie & the amazing Hemingway’s Team we thank you all for the good times and memories. Stay safe……and eat plants!! 🙂

[24/3/2023, 12:10:48 AM] Clodagh: Emotional reaction creates a refractory period. It's within this period that we take a snapshot of the cause of that emotion or the circumstance or experience that caused the emotion. The end result is a memory. These memories create a boundary of highs and lows.


When these refractory periods last hours or perhaps days the form "moods". If you allow these moods to last week's or months they become temperament. When mood become temperament they then become a personal trait.


70% of our life we spend living in survival or stress mode (mood) because our personality traits cause us to always anticipate the worst outcome based on this previous experience or snapshot. This heightened emotional state changes the entire physiology of the body which as a result create a higher level of stress, anxiety. Therefore, our emotional state is one both in mind and body.


We create this cycle of emotional recurrence. Our bodies have literally become hard wired to the heightened level of stress. It becomes addicted to the chemical release. We look at everyday struggles and our mind automatically catastrophize the situation so our brain produces the chemical that gives our addiction the hit it needs.

[13/4/2023, 11:22:48 PM] Clodagh: Emotional reaction creates a refractory period. It's within this period that we take a snapshot of the cause of that emotion or the circumstance or experience that caused the emotion. The end result is a memory. These memories create a boundary of highs and lows.


When these refractory periods last hours or perhaps days the form "moods". If you allow these moods to last week's or months they become temperament. When mood become temperament they then become a personal trait.


70% of our life we spend living in survival or stress mode (mood) because our personality traits cause us to always anticipate the worst outcome based on this previous experience or snapshot. This heightened emotional state changes the entire physiology of the body which as a result create a higher level of stress, anxiety. Therefore, our emotional state is one both in mind and body.


We create this cycle of emotional recurrence. Our bodies have literally become hard wired to the heightened level of stress. It becomes addicted to the chemical release. We look at everyday struggles and our mind automatically catastrophize the situation so our brain produces the chemical that gives our addiction the hit it needs.

[10/5/2024, 6:51:17 AM] Julian: In Hong Kong, if someone is convinced to lend money through deception, the offender has committed the crime of obtaining property by deception under Section 17 of the Theft Ordinance (Cap. 210).[1][4] This offense occurs when a person dishonestly obtains property belonging to another by deception, with the intention of permanently depriving the other person of that property.[4] Lending money would constitute "property" under the ordinance.

Specifically, if the offender deceives the victim into lending money, with the dishonest intention of not repaying the loan, this would amount to obtaining property (the money lent) by deception.[1][4] The key elements are the dishonest deception used to induce the lending, and the intention to permanently deprive the victim of the money lent.

The maximum penalty for obtaining property by deception is 10 years' imprisonment under Section 17 of the Theft Ordinance.[4] More severe penalties of up to 14 years' imprisonment and a HK$5 million fine can apply if the deception involves proceeds over HK$1 million under the Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance.[2]

[7/6/2024, 6:24:11 AM] Julian: Here are 10 fun Taylor Swift-themed activities or party games for a 10-year-old girl's birthday party:

1. **Karaoke Sing-Along**: Set up a karaoke machine with Taylor Swift songs for guests to sing along[1][2].

2. **Friendship Bracelet Making**: Provide a bead kit for guests to make their own friendship bracelets, which can also serve as party favors

3. **Dress Up in Your Eras Best**: Encourage guests to dress in outfits inspired by their favorite Taylor Swift era and hold a costume contest or fashion show

4. **Bejeweled Make-Overs**: Set up a beauty stand for sparkly makeovers with hair extensions and gem stickers

5. **Guess the Song Game**: Play short clips of Taylor Swift songs or read lyrics, and have guests guess the song or album

6. **Red Carpet Photobooth**: Create a photo booth with glitter streamers, a life-size Taylor cutout, and an instant camera for guests to take Polaroid pictures

7. **Shake It Off Game**: Cover kids with sticky notes and have them dance to "Shake It Off" to see who can lose the most notes in a set time

8. **Invisible String Obstacle Course**: Set up a string course with obstacles, where one child is blindfolded and guided by a partner[5].

9. **Movie Watch Party**: Stream "Taylor Swift | The Eras Tour" movie and have a dance floor for guests to enjoy[1].

10. **Taylor Swift Pictionary**: Create a Pictionary game using Taylor Swift song titles and lyrics for guests to draw and guess[1].

These activities will ensure a memorable and engaging Taylor Swift-themed birthday party.

Sources
[1] Taylor Swift Kids' Birthday Party Ideas to Celebrate Your Little Swiftie https://theeverymom.com/taylor-swift-kids-birthday-party-ideas/
[2] Epic Taylor Swift Birthday Party Ideas - One Hangry Mama https://onehangrymama.com/epic-taylor-swift-birthday-party-ideas/
[3] How to Throw a Taylor Swift Birthday Party - Crazy for Crust https://www.crazyforcrust.com/how-to-throw-a-taylor-swift-birthday-party/
[4] 51 Fun Taylor Swift Themed Party Activities, Outfits & More for 2024 https://www.classpop.com/magazine/taylor-swift-themed-party
[5] Birthday party ideas for Swiftie daughter : r/TaylorSwift - Reddit https://www.reddit.com/r/TaylorSwift/comments/14b2y0p/birthday_party_ideas_for_swiftie_daughter/

[8/6/2024, 1:35:05 PM] Clodagh: Here are some ideas for a Taylor Swift-themed scavenger hunt without using any copyrighted lyrics:

1. Find an item that is the same color as the album cover for one of Taylor's albums.

2. Take a photo of yourself in a location that matches the descriptions of a place mentioned in one of her songs (without using any lyrics).

3. Collect items that represent the themes or imagery commonly found in Taylor's music, such as hearts, stars, flowers, etc.

4. Search for clues that are related to the titles of Taylor's albums or singles (without quoting the titles).

5. Complete a task or challenge that is inspired by the storylines or emotions expressed in Taylor's music, described in your own words.

The key is to focus on the general themes, imagery and styles associated with Taylor Swift's artistry, rather than directly quoting or reproducing her copyrighted lyrics or other content. Get creative with original clues and challenges that capture the spirit of her music.

[19/10/2024, 12:03:12 PM] Julian: Dear All,

This year the HKFA are putting together a U12 Golden Age Girls League and we are  entering a HKJFL Girls Select team in this.
 
There are a total of 7 teams registered and the tournament will run from 16th November for 5 consecutive weeks.
On top of this we will look to send this team to an overseas tour before the season ends next year. We have been in touch with clubs in the HKJFL and your daughter has been put forward to do trials for this squad.   
 
Currently we have 20 girls put forward from the following clubs:   MLFA, HK Dragons, BFA, APSS, KCC and Tekkerz.  
 
Trials will take place on Tuesday 22nd October 4:30-6:00pm at the HKFA Training Centre, TKO and on Sunday 27th October 8:00-9:30am at Stanley Ho Sports Centre, Pokfulam. Please complete this FORM to advise your availability and to confirm your details . There will be a cost associated with this but we are trying to minimise it. For a home and away kit and tournament and coaching costs it will be HK$900 per player, but there is an option of receiving a refund of HK$400 at the end of the season if you want to return the kits at the end of the season.
 
We will try to arrange some friendly matches before the league starts and we will stop HKJFL league matches for the clubs involved during this period and just have friendly matches as a lot of the top players will be involved in this team. 
 
If you require any further information, please let us know through your club.
 

Kind regards / HKJFL

[4/8/2025, 6:02:46 PM] Julian: To check which devices are currently logged into your Instagram account (to see if anyone else, such as your partner, might have access), follow these steps:

1. **Open the Instagram app** on your phone.
2. **Go to your Profile** by tapping your profile icon in the bottom right corner.
3. **Tap the three lines (menu) in the top right corner.**
4. Select **Settings and Privacy**.
5. Tap **Account Center** at the top of the menu (if you don’t see this, make sure your Instagram app is updated).
6. Inside Account Center, tap **Password and Security**.
7. Look for the section called **Security Checks** and choose **Where You’re Logged In**.

Here you’ll see a list of every device that’s currently logged into your Instagram account, including device type and (usually) the location of recent access. If you spot devices or locations that you don’t recognize, you can select the device and choose to remove access (log it out). You can also change your password and enable two-factor authentication for added security[1][2][3][4].

These steps work on both iPhone and Android. Regularly checking this feature is a good practice to ensure your account remains secure.

Sources
[1] How To See All Instagram Logged In Devices https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8mQ2Scd9OKE
[2] How to Check Instagram Account Login Devices https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oeAFYeBnEkU
[3] How To Check What Devices Are Logged In To Instagram https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4t5zaMTyMOk
[4] View your recent login activity https://help.instagram.com/2761108904184084/?cms_platform=www&helpref=platform_switcher
[5] Here is the easiest way to tell which devices are logged ... https://www.instagram.com/reel/C2b3W3LIG3-/?hl=en
[6] View your account's recent login activity ... https://help.instagram.com/2761108904184084/?helpref=related_articles
[7] Add or remove Instagram login information on your device https://help.instagram.com/1020536697967549
[8] View your login history https://help.instagram.com/2761108904184084

[7/1/2026, 5:18:07 PM] Julian: This kind of decision really needs your prescriber’s input urgently, but from what is known about SSRIs like Lexapro, abruptly stopping for several days can cause withdrawal symptoms that often improve quickly if the medication is restarted, while staying off it risks those symptoms and possible mood relapse lingering into your interview.[1][2][3]

## Key points for your situation

- Stopping SSRIs suddenly can trigger a “discontinuation syndrome” with anxiety, low mood, brain fog, irritability, sleep problems and flu‑like symptoms that can appear within 1–4 days of the last dose.[4][2][1]
- Clinical guidance for antidepressant discontinuation generally recommends managing significant withdrawal by restarting the previous dose and then tapering more slowly later if needed, because symptoms often ease within 24–72 hours of reinstating the drug.[5][6][3]
- Brief treatment interruptions (a few days) are common non‑adherence patterns, and people do usually restart the same antidepressant, though dose and schedule should be confirmed with the prescriber, especially after more than a few days off.[7][8][9]

## How this maps to the next 4–5 days

- You are already in the window where withdrawal symptoms can be most intense (after 5 missed days), which matches your feeling that your well‑being has taken a hit.[10][11][2]
- If what you are feeling is mainly withdrawal rather than a full relapse of depression, restarting Lexapro at your usual dose often reduces these physical and emotional symptoms relatively quickly, sometimes within a couple of days, which could help your concentration by interview day.[6][3][5]
- Staying off completely is more likely to mean you endure unstable mood, anxiety, and cognitive fog through the interview period, because acute withdrawal can last 1–6 weeks in some people.[11][2][1]

## Practical next steps (urgent)

- **Contact a doctor today** (GP, psychiatrist, out‑of‑hours or telehealth if needed) to:  
  - Confirm that you should restart now and at what dose (sometimes they may suggest restarting slightly lower if you have been off for several days).[12][13][7]
  - Document any previous side effects or early‑treatment jitteriness you had when you first started Lexapro, since that informs whether a full or reduced restart dose makes sense.[8][7]
- If you cannot reach your usual prescriber, NHS/urgent care or a local mental health helpline can advise how to get same‑day review, especially given you have both a psychiatric medicine and a significant physical condition (essential thrombocythaemia on peginterferon).[14][15][16]

## Managing the interview days themselves

These are non‑drug tactics you can use regardless of the medication plan to reduce emotional volatility and preserve focus:

- For the next 4–5 days, use a **tight routine**: fixed wake time, light exercise, regular meals, and a strict caffeine cutoff early afternoon, which can reduce both withdrawal jitteriness and fatigue.[1][4]
- Prepare a **scripted interview plan**: key stories, bullet‑point answers for likely questions, and a simple “if mind goes blank, say X” recovery line, so you rely less on emotional state and more on rehearsed structure.[17]
- Use brief, evidence‑based calming techniques before and on the day: 5–10 minutes of slow breathing or a short walk, rather than heavy last‑minute cramming.[4][1]

## Safety flags

- Seek urgent medical help or emergency services if you notice severe worsening mood, suicidal thoughts, extreme agitation, or confusion; these can occur during abrupt SSRI changes and must be taken very seriously.[2][1][4]

In summary, in most situations like yours the safer and more stabilizing approach is to restart the medication promptly under medical guidance rather than stay off it through the interview, while using structured preparation and short‑term coping strategies to support performance.[3][5][6]

[20/5/2026, 3:23:59 PM] Julian: You’re probably thinking of **hepatic encephalopathy** – a brain problem caused by the liver not clearing toxins properly, often after liver damage from alcohol or other causes.[1][2][3]

## What it is

- Hepatic encephalopathy happens when a damaged liver can’t filter toxins (especially ammonia from the gut) out of the blood, so they build up and affect the brain.[2][3][1]
- It is most often seen in people with cirrhosis or advanced liver disease, including alcohol‑related liver disease.[3][4][1]

## Symptoms (including hallucinations)

- Typical symptoms include confusion, disorientation, trouble concentrating, personality changes, sleep–wake reversal, and in severe cases coma.[4][1][2][3]
- Some patients also experience visual or other hallucinations when the brain is significantly affected, and people may appear “drunk,” agitated, or very out of character.[5][6][3]

## Why alcohol or food can trigger it

- Protein in food and alcohol metabolism both increase production of substances like ammonia in the gut and bloodstream; if the liver is damaged, it cannot break these down normally.[7][8][1][3]
- This is why someone with cirrhosis may suddenly become confused or hallucinate after drinking alcohol, bleeding in the gut, constipation, infection, or a big dietary change.[1][3]

If you’re asking because you or someone you know is having new confusion or hallucinations and might have liver disease, this is considered an emergency and needs same‑day medical assessment. Would you like a quick checklist of “red flag” symptoms that mean you should go straight to A&E right now?

[5/6/2026, 9:31:07 AM] Julian: You probably do **not** need to make a police report just because you lost the temporary paper acknowledgement before collecting your new HKID. The Immigration Department’s published collection rules say the acknowledgement of application should be returned at collection, while a passport is accepted as valid proof of identity in various ID-related procedures; however, the official pages I found do not say that a police report is mandatory for a lost acknowledgement slip before collection. [gov](https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/immigration/others/loseid.htm)

## What the rules say

For a lost HKID, the official rule is that you must report the loss and apply for a replacement at a Registration of Persons Office within 14 days.  That requirement is clearly about the **identity card itself**, and the Immigration Department also says that if a lost identity card is later recovered, it should be returned to a Registration of Persons Office or police station. [gov](https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/immigration/others/loseid.htm)

For collection of a new HKID, the Immigration Department says the applicant should collect it in person within the period stated on the acknowledgement, and must return the acknowledgement of application upon collection. You should definitely bring your **passport** or other valid travel document, because the Immigration Department explicitly treats a passport as valid proof of identity for identity-card related matters and for travel when someone only holds an acknowledgement of application. [immd.gov](https://www.immd.gov.hk/eng/services/hkid/reg_replace.html)

## Practical next step

Because the official pages do not explicitly cover the exact scenario of a **lost paper acknowledgement before card collection**, the safest course is to go to the relevant Registration of Persons Office with your passport and the HKID photocopy, explain that the acknowledgement slip was lost, and let them verify your identity from their records.  If you want to avoid a wasted trip, call the Immigration Department first at 2824 6111 and ask whether they want any extra declaration or replacement acknowledgement before collection. [gov](https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/immigration/others/loseid.htm)

Based on the official material I found, a police report does **not appear to be expressly required** before collecting the permanent card in your situation.  So in practice, your passport is the key document to bring, and the photocopy of the old HKID may help, but the final check is at the counter because the acknowledgement slip is normally supposed to be surrendered at collection.
